scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: Hello, one workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- seems to have fallen off the network entirely. From
that desk you can't reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the
usual first stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine.
Nothing was moved or changed as far as anyone remembers. Could someone have a
look at why just PC11 is cut off and put it back on? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation of PC11 and its supporting infrastructure found no fault. Every diagnostic test produced normal results:

**L1/L2**: PC11's eth0 is UP with the correct MAC (4e:6b:14:fe:03:56). On switch2, port eth5 is UP and correctly a member of the br_vlan20 bridge — the same bridge holding PC9 (eth3) and PC10 (eth4). No misconfigured PVID or wrong-VLAN assignment was found.

**L3 local**: PC11 holds the correct address 172.16.20.11/24 and default gateway 172.16.20.254. It pings both same-VLAN neighbours PC9 (172.16.20.9) and PC10 (172.16.20.10) with 0% loss, and reaches the gateway on mswitch0's vlan20 SVI with 0% loss.

**L3 inter-VLAN**: PC11 successfully reaches VLAN10 hosts (172.16.10.5, via mswitch0) and VLAN30 hosts (172.16.30.12/13) — identical results to PC10 running the same tests. mswitch0 carries correct OSPF-learned routes and has no iptables or ebtables rules that would selectively block PC11.

**VLAN5 unreachable**: Neither PC11 nor PC10 can reach 172.16.5.x. This is a topology design boundary: mswitch0 has no route to 172.16.5.0/24 (VLAN5 machines live behind sshswitch/router17, a separate L3 domain). This is equal for every VLAN20 host and is not a defect.

**Root cause**: There is no anomaly. PC11 is fully operational. The helpdesk report is a false premise — no actual outage or misconfiguration exists for PC11 or its switch port.

**Corrective action**: No change required. If the reporter observed a transient issue, it has self-resolved; otherwise the report may have been submitted in error.
